claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from the SAFHS cohort (n=1,240) showed that 1,143 transcripts were positively correlated and 1,142 transcripts were negatively correlated with chronological age compared to younger age.

sources.quote: Using a cutoff of adjusted P≤0.05 (with the Benjamini–Hochberg method to correct for multiple testing), we identified 1,143 and 1,142 transcripts positively and negatively correlated to age, respectively, in the SAFHS data set (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Table 3a).

Figure 2 | Development of the BioAge signature and application to the EM131 cohort. (a) Expression of the 2,285 age-related transcripts derived from SAFHS data set (n = 1,240)19; all transcripts correlating with chronological age (moderated t-test: adjusted P≤0.05) were clustered in 20 modules using k-means clustering.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy participants showed that pathways regulating cell motility, integrin signalling, type II interferon signalling, complement-related inflammatory responses, and T-cell/natural killer-cell-mediated cytolysis were enriched in elderly participants compared to younger participants.

sources.quote: On the one hand, pathways positively associated with older age included pathways that regulate cell motility (M12 and M14) and genes downstream of integrin signalling (M15). A type II interferon signalling module (M17) characterized by the induced expression of TNF and IFNG was also enriched in elderly participants. Inflammatory responses that include complement genes (M16) downstream of interferons, as well as T-cell/natural killer (NK)-cells-mediated cytolysis (M19) markers such as perforin and granzyme B, were also positively associated with older age.

claim_3.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy participants showed that B-cell signalling, T-cell receptor signalling, antiviral response, MYC signalling, amino acid metabolism, fatty acid biosynthesis, and lipid metabolic pathways were enriched in younger participants compared to elderly participants.

sources.quote: On the other hand, pathways enriched in younger participants included immunological pathways such as B-cell signalling (M1) comprising several B-cell markers (CD79A, CD79B, CD19, CD20 and CD22), T-cell receptor signalling (M6) that included ZAP70, TRAF1, TCF7 a marker of memory T cells20 and antiviral response (M8) that included the antiviral signalling gene MAVS. MYC signalling (M3), which triggers metabolic pathways such as amino acid metabolism (M2 and M4), fatty acid biosynthesis (M9) and lipid metabolic pathways (M11), all critical for the induction of T- and B-cell memory, was enriched in younger participants.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood cells from the EM131 cohort showed that chronological age was associated with the BioAge score compared to younger age.

sources.quote: There was a statistically significant association between chronological age and BioAge on the EM131 cohort (Fig. 2c, Wilcoxon rank-sum test: P = 1.01e−05), confirming the validity of this score to reflect the impact of age on gene expression in whole blood cells.

Figure 2 | Development of the BioAge signature and application to the EM131 cohort. (c) Scatter plot showing the chronological age as a function of the BioAge. The vertical line indicates a BioAge score of 0. We observe that young participants (red circles) have significantly younger BioAge; and among elderly (black circles) about half of participants have a young BioAge (<0) while the other half have an old BioAge (oAge).

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood cells from elderly participants in the EM131 cohort before vaccination showed that the BioAge score was associated with the rate of response to the HBV vaccine compared to BioAge young elderly participants.

sources.quote: Both the BioAge score (Supplementary Fig. 3) and the two groups of elderly identified by the BioAge signature (Fisher’s exact test: odds ratio (OR) = 2.14, P = 0.0357; Fig. 3a) were associated with the rate of response to the HBV vaccine.

Figure 3 | BioAge predicts HBV vaccine response. (a) BioAge classification of the 135 elderly patients based on gene expression prior to vaccination is significantly associated with the response to HBV vaccination.

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood cells from elderly participants in the EM131 cohort before vaccination showed that lower expression of module M1 and higher expression of module M16 predicted response to the HBV vaccine compared to other BioAge modules.

sources.quote: Among the 20 gene modules defined in the BioAge signature, 2 modules M1 (lower expression in BioAge old) and M16 (high expression in BioAge old) allowed the most accurate prediction of the response to the HBV vaccine (Fig. 3b).

Figure 3 | BioAge predicts HBV vaccine response. (b) Forward selection among the modules composing the BioAge signature resulted in the selection of modules M1 and M16 as optimal signatures, predicting HBV vaccine response in the EM131 elderly cohort (age≥65).

claim_7.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood cells from the EM131 elderly cohort before vaccination showed that the BioAge signature predicted the response to the HBV vaccine with 60.0% accuracy compared to chance.

sources.quote: To test the accuracy of this signature, we performed a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis that indicated that the BioAge signature could predict the response to the HBV vaccine with an accuracy of 60.0% in the EM131 elderly cohort (Fig. 3b, permutation test: P = 0.0163).

Figure 3 | BioAge predicts HBV vaccine response. (b) Forward selection among the modules composing the BioAge signature resulted in the selection of modules M1 and M16 as optimal signatures, predicting HBV vaccine response in the EM131 elderly cohort (age≥65).

claim_8.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the EM131 elderly cohort before vaccination showed no single transcript was significantly differentially expressed between HBV vaccine responders and poor-responders compared to the other group.

sources.quote: We were not able to identify a single transcript that was significantly differentially expressed between HBV vaccine responders and poor-responders of the EM131 training set (linear model for microarray (LIMMA): adjusted P≤0.05, Supplementary Table 4a).

claim_9.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the EM131 elderly training and test cohorts before vaccination showed that a naive Bayes classifier based on the top 15 differentially expressed genes predicted the response to the HBV vaccine with 62.6% accuracy in the training set and 62.2% accuracy in the test set compared to chance.

sources.quote: The accuracy of the resulting 15-gene signature was assessed on the EM131 training set by 10-fold cross-validation and on the EM131 test set and found to be 62.6% and 62.2%, respectively (Fig. 4b,c, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 4b).

Figure 4 | Identification of gene-expression signature predicting the HBV vaccine response. (c) ROC curve and area under the curve (AUC) for the prediction of the HBV vaccine response using the 15-gene signature on the EM131 test set (n = 49).

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the EM131 elderly cohort before vaccination showed that the 15-gene signature and the BioAge signature shared members of the B-cell signalling and inflammation pathways compared to non-overlapping pathways.

sources.quote: Network inference revealed that both the 15-gene signature and the BioAge signature shared members of the B-cell signalling (CD20, BANK1; Fisher’s exact test: P = 7.99e−07) and inflammation pathways (Fig. 4e).

Figure 4 | Identification of gene-expression signature predicting the HBV vaccine response. (e) Networks were inferred for the BioAge module 1 combined to the 15-gene signature and the BioAge module 16 combined to the 15-gene signature, respectively.

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the EM131 elderly cohort before vaccination showed that B-cell signalling was positively associated with response to HBV vaccine, whereas inflammation-associated genes including IRF7 and HP were associated with lower antibody titres.

sources.quote: Both signatures showed upregulated expression of genes directly associated with inflammation. In the BioAge M16, IRF7 (the master switch of type I interferon) and its downstream targets IL-15 and OAS1, as well as NFkB and C1 (hallmarks of inflammation) were associated with lower Ab titres. In the 15-gene signature, haptoglobin (HP), an acute phase protein and also a target gene of type I interferon signalling, was associated with low Ab titres. Pathway analysis performed on a list of genes derived with a less stringent statistical cutoff of nominal P≤0.05 confirmed the positive association of B-cell signalling and the response to HBV vaccine

claim_12.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of pre-vaccination blood from the EM131 training set showed that frequencies of switched IgG+ memory B cells and IgG+ memory B cells predicted response to the HBV vaccine compared to poor-responders.

sources.quote: Two cell subsets defined by FCM, namely frequencies of switched IgG+ memory B cells (CD3−, CD19+, HLADR+, CD27+, IgG+) and of IgG+ memory B cells (CD3−, CD19+, HLADR+, CD27+, CD10−, CD20+, IgG+) were identified as significant predictors of the response to the HBV vaccine (Fig. 5a and Table 1).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. Polychromatic FCM was used to identify cell surface markers of the response to the HBV vaccine. (a) Box plots presenting the frequencies of the four FCM markers selected in the forward selection model in responders and poor-responders to the HBV vaccine on the EM131 training set (n = 95).

claim_13.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of pre-vaccination blood from the EM131 training set showed that frequencies of CD4 T-effector memory 2 cells and CD40 on plasmacytoid dendritic cells were negatively associated with HBV vaccine response compared to responders.

sources.quote: Frequencies of CD4 T-effector memory 2 (CD28−, marker of immunosenescence24) and CD40 on plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), another byproduct of chronic immune activation and inflammation25, correlated negatively with HBV vaccine response (Fig. 5a).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. Polychromatic FCM was used to identify cell surface markers of the response to the HBV vaccine. (a) Box plots presenting the frequencies of the four FCM markers selected in the forward selection model in responders and poor-responders to the HBV vaccine on the EM131 training set (n = 95).

claim_14.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of pre-vaccination blood from the EM131 training and test sets showed that a multivariate model combining switched IgG+ memory B cells, IgG+ memory B cells, CD4 T-effector memory 2, and CD40 in pDCs predicted the response to HBV vaccine with an accuracy of 63.3% compared to chance.

sources.quote: A multivariate regression model combining four FCM markers (% switched IgG+ memory B cells, % IgG+ memory B cells, % CD4 T-effector memory 2 and the median fluorescence intensity of CD40 in pDCs; Table 1), trained on the EM131 training set, was able to predict the response to HBV vaccine in the test set with an accuracy of 63.3% (Fig. 5b, permutation test: P = 0.0468).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. Polychromatic FCM was used to identify cell surface markers of the response to the HBV vaccine. (b) ROC curves for the prediction of the HBV vaccine response using the FCM data on the EM131 test set.

claim_15.claim: Multiplex ELISA analysis of pre-vaccination serum from the EM131 training set showed that IL-15, IL-1ra, and TNFR2 were negatively associated with HBV vaccine response compared to responders.

assay.name_in_paper: multiplex ELISA protocol Human Inflammation multianalyte profiling

sources.quote: Three inflammation-associated proteins—IL-15, IL-1ra and TNFR2—were negatively associated with HBV vaccine response on the EM131 training set (Supplementary Table 5b,c and Supplementary Fig. 5b).

claim_16.claim: Multiplex ELISA analysis of pre-vaccination serum from the EM131 test set showed that the cytokine model was not significantly associated with HBV vaccine response compared to responders.

assay.name_in_paper: multiplex ELISA protocol Human Inflammation multianalyte profiling

sources.quote: This model was not significantly associated to the HBV vaccine response in the EM131 test set (Supplementary Fig. 5c, permutation test: P = 0.250).

claim_17.claim: Haematologic measurements analysis of pre-vaccination blood from elderly participants showed that higher red blood cell counts were associated with low antibody titres compared to lower red blood cell counts.

sources.quote: Interestingly, higher red blood cell (RBC) counts were associated with low Ab titres in elderly (Table 1 and Fig. 5c,d).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. (c) Box plots presenting the RBC counts (measured in a 28-day window prior to HBV vaccination) in responders and poor-responders to the HBV vaccine on the EM131 training set (n = 95). (d) ROC curves illustrating the prediction of the HBV vaccine response using RBC counts on the EM131 test set.

claim_18.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from elderly participants before vaccination, using least-square regression integration with flow cytometry, showed that the BioAge module M1 and the 15-gene signature were positively associated with frequencies of memory B cells and increased CD4 counts.

sources.quote: Results of this analysis showed that the two independently derived B-cell gene-expression signatures (that is, the BioAge module M1 and the 15-gene signature) were correlated with frequencies of memory B cells identified by FCM and with increased CD4 counts.

Figure 6 | Integrative analysis reveals positive correlations between biomarkers of HBV vaccine response. A projection-based multivariate approach was adopted to assess the correlation between transcriptomic, FCM, haematologic and cytokine/chemokine expression data sets.

claim_19.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from elderly participants before vaccination, using least-square regression integration with flow cytometry, showed that the inflammation gene-expression signature including C1QB, C3, and IRF7 was positively associated with activated innate immune cell markers and immunosenescent CD4 T cells.

sources.quote: Conversely the gene-expression signature of inflammation (for example, C1QB, C3, IRF7) correlated positively with FCM markers of activated innate immune cells and immunosenescent CD4 T cells (TEM2 in CD4s, CD40 in mDC1s and CD40 in pDCs, respectively) (Fig. 6).

Figure 6 | Integrative analysis reveals positive correlations between biomarkers of HBV vaccine response. A projection-based multivariate approach was adopted to assess the correlation between transcriptomic, FCM, haematologic and cytokine/chemokine expression data sets.

claim_20.claim: Multiplex ELISA analysis of serum from elderly participants before vaccination, using least-square regression integration with flow cytometry, showed that heightened levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines including SCF, TNFR2, and VEGF were positively associated with increased frequencies of activated innate immune cells.

assay.name_in_paper: multiplex ELISA protocol Human Inflammation multianalyte profiling

sources.quote: This integrated analysis showed the correlation between heightened levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (for example, SCF, TNFR2 and VEGF) and increased frequencies of activated innate immune cells (TEM2 in CD4s, CD40 in mDC1s and CD40 in pDCs, respectively).

Figure 6 | Integrative analysis reveals positive correlations between biomarkers of HBV vaccine response. A projection-based multivariate approach was adopted to assess the correlation between transcriptomic, FCM, haematologic and cytokine/chemokine expression data sets.

claim_21.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that MYD88 and TRAF were negatively associated with the frequency of CD4 T cells compared to higher CD4 T-cell frequency.

sources.quote: Both MYD88 and TRAF are negatively correlated to the frequency of CD4 T cells, a marker of good response to HBV vaccination (Supplementary Fig. 6b, Pearson’s correlation: r = −0.347 P<0.05 and r = −0.353 P<0.05, respectively).

claim_22.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that C3 and WARS were negatively associated with the frequencies of the two memory B-cell subsets compared to higher memory B-cell frequencies.

sources.quote: Moreover, C3 and WARS, two target genes of type I interferons, were negatively associated to the frequencies of the two memory B-cell subsets.

claim_23.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that CD200 and BATF3 were repressed in HBV vaccine hyporesponders compared to responders.

sources.quote: In contrast, anti-inflammatory protein-coding genes like CD200 (ref. 32) and BATF3 (ref. 33) were repressed in HBV vaccine hyporesponders (Fig. 6).

Figure 6 | Integrative analysis reveals positive correlations between biomarkers of HBV vaccine response. A projection-based multivariate approach was adopted to assess the correlation between transcriptomic, FCM, haematologic and cytokine/chemokine expression data sets.

claim_24.claim: Haematologic measurements analysis of blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that poor-responders had higher numbers of red blood cells than responders.

sources.quote: Poor-responders to HBV vaccine showed higher numbers of RBCs than responders.

claim_25.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that genes and pathways positively correlated with HBV antibody titres, including genes within module M1, were negatively associated with red blood cell counts, whereas genes included in module M16 and pro-inflammatory genes enriched in poor-responders were positively associated with red blood cell counts.

sources.quote: Interestingly genes and pathways that correlate positively with HBV Ab titres including genes within module M1 were negatively correlated with RBC counts. Conversely genes included in module M16 (Fig. 6) and pro-inflammatory genes included in pathways enriched in poor-responders (Fig. 5e) were positive correlates of RBC counts.

claim_26.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that the HIF-1α pathway was upregulated in poor-responders compared to responders.

sources.quote: The HIF-1α pathway. which controls erythropoietin expression, was significantly upregulated in poor-responders (Fisher’s exact test: P = 0.0360, Supplementary Table 4c); target genes of HIF-1α were induced in poor-responders and their expression levels correlated with higher RBC counts (Pearson’s t-test: P = 0.0462, Fig. 5e).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. (e) Heat map representation of the genes differentially expressed between HBV vaccine R and PR overlapping the HIF-1α canonical pathway in the training set.

claim_27.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that HIF-1α target gene expression was positively associated with higher red blood cell counts.

sources.quote: The HIF-1α pathway. which controls erythropoietin expression, was significantly upregulated in poor-responders (Fisher’s exact test: P = 0.0360, Supplementary Table 4c); target genes of HIF-1α were induced in poor-responders and their expression levels correlated with higher RBC counts (Pearson’s t-test: P = 0.0462, Fig. 5e).

Figure 5 | B-cell subset as well as innate immune cell subsets and RBC counts are predictive of the response to the HBV vaccine. (e) Heat map representation of the genes differentially expressed between HBV vaccine R and PR overlapping the HIF-1α canonical pathway in the training set. The P value of t-test between RBC and the ordering of the samples is 0.0462.

claim_28.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that red blood cell counts were positively associated with HMOX1, HP, and CD163 expression compared to lower red blood cell counts.

sources.quote: RBC counts were positively correlated to the HMOX1 (haem oxidase catalysing the degradation of haem), HP (scavenger of free Hb) and CD163 expressions (scavenger receptor of the Hb–HP complex), all of which are interferon-regulated genes and were induced in HBV vaccine poor-responders (Supplementary Table 4a).

claim_29.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that the haem-induced response pathway was enriched in poor-responders compared to responders.

sources.quote: The haem-induced response pathway was significantly enriched among genes differentially expressed between HBV vaccine responders and poor-responders (Fisher’s exact test: P = 0.0461, Supplementary Table 4c).

claim_30.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from poor-responders and responders before vaccination showed that EIF2AK1 and several of its downstream targets including EIF2, EIF3, and EIF4 were negatively associated with antibody titres.

sources.quote: EIF2AK1 (Haem-Regulated Inhibitor) and several of its downstream targets (for example, EIF2, EIF3 and EIF4) were negatively associated with Ab titres (Supplementary Fig. 6a).
